reason: Boat-shaped (navicular) leaves are normal in mosses. One example is a bract, but the pair holds.
Seeds have margins and ends that can be entire or toothed. The examples read as the seed margin.
Tongue-shaped (ligulate) stigmas are strap-shaped. This is correct.
A leaf blade can be striate (fine parallel lines).
This is a count of epicalyx bracts. It fits the counted-parts rule.
Embryo shape (straight or curved) is standard.
A subglobose involucre is spheroid. This is correct.
Velvety hairs on the lower leaf surface are valid. The epidermis stands in for the surface.
'Capsules mature May-June' gives the time of ripening (phenology). It does not describe the capsule's quality. A rule should send it to phenology.
Persistent tepals are non-deciduous. This is correct.
A lamina apex can be bilobed. The part is the apex of the blade.
Granular ornamentation of spore or perispore surfaces is a normal surface texture.
Flower buds are often conical. This is correct.
A club-shaped ovary is valid.
'structure' is too generic to describe anything. The examples (bordered, articulations, striolate) need specific terms or has-part patterns.
Calyptra present or absent is meaningful. But 'not seen' or 'not observed' means unknown, not absent. A rule must treat 'not seen' as no data.
Achenes are often hispidulous (finely bristly).
Suberect styles are semi-erect. This is correct.
A length-to-width ratio of a corolla or its lip is meaningful. The ratio must be kept as a number or comparison.
'Cells irregularly arranged' is a pattern, which fits. But 'irregularly to linear-rectangular' and 'upper cells irregular' are shape. A rule must tell arrangement from shape.
A sepal or its apex can be expanded or dilated. Margin-specific cases would need the margin as the part.
Orbicular achenes are valid.
Shiny involucral bracts are valid. One example is only a patch of the bract.
Scaly (lepidote) seeds occur. The examples are correct.
'characteristic' is the root quality and says nothing. The examples (slender/stout, simple/branched) need specific thickness or branching terms.
A leathery perigynium is valid.
'Spurred petal' means the petal has a spur, so it should be a has-part spur. It does not mean the petal is spur-shaped.
Pollinia colour is valid.
Suberect or semi-erect fruits and capsules are valid.
A stigma wider than its style, or widened at the base, is a valid width.
Turions present or absent is a normal presence statement.
Peduncles are often floccose (woolly).
A coriaceous (leathery) tunic is valid.
'Perichaetial leaves undifferentiated' fits leaf. But 'alar cells not differentiated' is about cells. A rule must send cell examples to the cell part.
A deeply divided sepal or sepal margin is valid.
'Compressed' means flattened, a shape. PATO condensed means compacted. The two readings differ. A flattened or compressed shape term is needed.
'Abundant' usually describes how many hairs the organ bears, not a quality of the hair itself. A rule would need to attach it to the organ's indumentum density.
Cylindrical mericarps are valid.
Ovule length is valid.
A small or minute aril is valid.
'characteristic' is the root quality. Included or exserted, and glabrous or gland-dotted, need specific terms.
'Spatial pattern' is too generic. 'Paired' or 'binate' needs a specific arrangement term. Spreading also belongs to orientation.
Keeled sporophylls are valid.
Glabrous floral bracts are valid.
Truncate apex, margin or lobe is valid.
A shallow calyx or calyx tube is valid.
Emarginate apex or lobe is valid.
Sericeous (silky) bracteoles are valid.
Small or minute stamens are valid.
Elliptic utricles are valid.
Concave faces of a nut are valid. The faces are a sub-part of the nut.
Spreading lobes are valid.
'Extended through 1/3-2/3 of the spur' gives how far the nectary reaches into the spur. It does not extend beyond anything. This is a wrong reading.
The examples describe a twisted beak (rostre), not the keel. The part is wrong.
The examples describe a floral spur, not a short shoot. The part is wrong.
'Veins obsolete' means indistinct. PATO vestigial means a reduced remnant. A rule must map obsolete veins to the right term, not just to vascular bundle.
An involute leaflet or leaflet margin is valid.
A toothed or denticulate leaf apex is valid.
'Rays whorled' describes umbel rays (branches), not ray flowers. The part is wrong.
A thickened midrib or other structure is valid.
